A mosquito lands on your arm. How many would it take to drain all your blood?
A big swarm sounds like it could do it.
Only females bite, and each sips a drop smaller than a grain of rice.
Your body holds about five litres of blood, roughly a big jug.
Fill that jug one tiny drop at a time, and you'd need about a million mosquitoes.
Real danger comes sooner: after around four hundred thousand bites, you'd lose enough blood to be in serious trouble.
Luckily, you'd swat, scratch and run long before that.
So next time one bites you, relax. It's just one sip out of a million.
